dissent.summary: implement-with-changes. Phase 1 is too large and its acceptance command passes vacuously for un-enforced AI workers. Phase 2's acceptance command contains an escape hatch that makes it unfalsifiable. The claim that an empty diff is exempt in forjar is false, as the script explicitly rejects it. The quorum CI job must check out the base branch's script to prevent PR authors from bypassing the required check, and it must not use `if` or `paths` filters to skip runs for bots since skipped required checks block PRs.

findings.claim: KILL: [phase 1] A_1 is not properly falsifiable because the AI worker running the acceptance command is not in the enforced list; the gate will fall back to advisory mode and exit 0 even if diff_sha256 is altered, resulting in a vacuous pass. Also, Phase 1 is too large (porting 3 scripts, the spec, tests, and hooks) and exceeds 35 tool calls.
findings.fix: Split phase 1 into 1a (scripts/hooks) and 1b (tests/spec). In A_1, explicitly set QUORUM_ACTOR=noah@paiml.com in the environment so the gate runs in blocking mode and legitimately fails with exit 1 on a bad receipt.

findings.claim: KILL: [phase 2] A_2 is unfalsifiable because "or the receipt records the refusal" is an escape hatch allowing the worker to pass vacuously without the operator adding the check. Additionally, "workflow green on this PR" will pass vacuously for the AI worker since it is an advisory actor.
findings.fix: Remove the "or the receipt records the refusal" escape hatch from A_2. Require the workflow to be tested in blocking mode (e.g., by spoofing QUORUM_ACTOR) to prove it goes red on a bad receipt before passing on a good one.

findings.claim: KILL: [section 1 row 2 pre-push + quorum.yml] The claim "empty diff exempt" is false for forjar. quorum-gate.sh explicitly dies with exit 1 when the diff is empty but HEAD is ahead of the merge-base (a deletion is exempt, but an empty diff is rejected).
findings.fix: Change "empty diff exempt" to "empty diff rejected" or "deletion exempt".

findings.claim: ACCEPT: [ruleset required check] (i) dependabot PRs: passed vacuously (actor dependabot[bot] is not in enforced_for, gate falls to advisory and exits 0). (ii) operator docs PRs: blocked (unless a receipt is provided, as the operator is enforced). (iii) release PRs: blocked. [X] Workflows triggered by GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger other workflows; since the workflow never runs, the required check stays pending and blocks the PR. (iv) kind: triage PRs: blocked (without receipt) or passed (with receipt). (v) PRs from forks: passed vacuously (advisory exits 0), UNLESS [X] it's a first-time contributor requiring maintainer approval, where the workflow never runs until approved, blocking the PR.
findings.fix: Because [X] a skipped required status check remains Pending and blocks the PR, bashrs's quorum.yml MUST NOT attempt to optimize by adding 'if: github.actor != dependabot[bot]' or 'paths:' filters; it must always run and exit 0 for exempt actors. To prevent an enforced author from bypassing the required check by simply altering scripts/quorum-gate.sh in their PR, bashrs's quorum.yml MUST check out and run the gate script from the trusted base branch (e.g., github.base_ref), rather than executing the PR's version. enforce.json must remain identical to forjar's.

dissent.summary: do-not-implement-as-written. Phase 4 lacks a red run and cannot pass vacuously. Phase 7 reshaping old receipts is dead work because Gate A won't scan them. Ordering 3b's dependency on Phase 7 is thus flawed. Harness.sh correctly requires the IMPL marker and exactly one verdict line. Gate T correctly re-derives next.due and tracks release goals. Release-audit correctly asserts each release describes itself. Publish-from-tag correctly enforces a clean detached worktree. The dogfood skill name check prevents user-scope shadowing. Release-check correctly reports PENDING pre-tag. The falsification test count is 293 files and 1 directory, not 294 files.

findings.fix: Correct the ordering rationale; Gate A's execution on new PRs does not depend on the retroactive receipt reshaping of Phase 7.
